title: GOMS-KLM: Predicting Task Time
intro: A forty-year-old method that still beats guesswork: predict how long an expert takes to complete a task, without recruiting anyone.

learn.title: What the letters mean
learn.text:
**Goals** — what the user wants to achieve
**Operators** — keystroke, point, click, mental preparation
**Methods** — sequences of operators that accomplish a goal
**Selection rules** — which method applies in which context

**KLM** assigns a standard time to each operator. Developed at Xerox PARC and Carnegie Mellon, and replicated for decades.

options: Average time for a new user
The number of errors in a flow

learn.title: Five steps
learn.text:
**1. Define the workflow** — pick top tasks
**2. Identify goals and methods** — including alternatives, such as menu versus keyboard shortcut
**3. List operators** — every keystroke, pointer move, click and mental preparation
**4. Assign times and total** — use a template, and include system response time
**5. Validate and improve** — spot-check against real timings

Calabro reports it predicts skilled task time within **10–20%**.

try.q: How accurate does Calabro report the predictions to be?
try.explain: Close enough to compare designs and prioritise work.

learn.title: Where it fits, and where it doesn't
learn.text:
**Good for:** comparing two designs before building, prioritising efficiency work in high-repetition tasks, and settling “is this faster?” arguments without recruiting.

**Not for:** learnability, error recovery, satisfaction, or anything involving a novice — it models an expert who makes no mistakes.

*A related 2025 post compared GOMS-KLM with ChatGPT estimates; that comparison is tied to the model of the day.*

try.explain: It models an expert performing the task error-free.

options: A rule for choosing a method
test.explain: KLM assigns each a standard time. Pointer move or mental step.

test.q: Why include alternative methods in step 2?
options: Users may take the menu or the shortcut
To test both novice and expert paths
test.explain: Different routes have different predicted times.

test.q: What should you add beyond the human operators?
test.explain: The system's own delays count toward the task.

test.q: Which question can GOMS-KLM answer without recruiting?
options: Which of two designs is faster for an expert
Which design is easier to learn
